The Treaty of Lausanne was signed in Lau.why: Common-sense case: people say where a treaty was signed (the city) and where the city lies; nobody names the country of signing on its own, since the city already says it. It follows by chaining the two links with the removed rule.

sources.quote: The Treaty of Lausanne (French: Traité de Lausanne; Turkish: Lozan Antlaşması) is a peace treaty negotiated during the Lausanne Conference of 1922–1923 and signed in the Palais de Rumine in Lausanne, Switzerland, on 24 July 1923.

The treaty officially resolved the conflict that had initially arisen between the Ottoman Empire and the Allied French Republic, British Empire, Kingdom of Italy, Empire of Japan, Kingdom of Greece, Kingdom of Yugoslavia, and the Kingdom of Romania since the outset of World War I.

notes: RBox contraction paired with history-replace-0017: removes the original role chain, signed_in composed with located_in implies signed_in (the revision retargets it to 'was a party to'); signed_in carries chain:located_in->signed_in in RELATIONS.md. Every query becomes 'I don't know', including the three propositional ones (strong Kleene); the negation and compound questions state the chain as a plain sentence. The instance prompts say 'Given only these facts' (Lausanne 1923 and Switzerland; Paris 1898 and France) and ask whether the treaty was signed in the country. Near and far unrelated queries are the revision's (near exempt from Rule 7). Caveat: 'in Lausanne' already gives 'in Switzerland' by what 'in' means, so the chain is close to definitional and a 'yes' may be word sense kept.
